title: Being polite
body: English speakers say please and thank you a lot. "Thanks" is the casual form of "thank you". Answer a thank you with "You're welcome".

title: I am, you are, he is
body: The verb "to be" changes with the person: I am, you are, he is, she is. In speech it is usually short: I'm, you're, he's, she's.

title: Telling the time
body: For full hours, say "It is ... o'clock". "O'clock" is only used with whole hours: it is two o'clock, but it is two thirty.

title: Ordering politely
body: "I would like" (short: I'd like) is the polite way to ask for something. Add "please" at the end.

title: Describing people
body: English describing words never change: a tall man, a tall woman, tall people. They come after "is" or before the noun.

title: I work or I am working?
body: Use the simple form for habits (I work every day) and "am + -ing" for what is happening now (I am reading a book).

title: Very and too
body: "Very" makes a word stronger: very good. "Too" means more than you want: too expensive.
